title: Bridge-hire risk and activation protocol
body:
Purpose:
This doc outlines a compact protocol for 'bridge hires' — candidates onboarded on a fixed trial/reserve period (typically 60-90 days) before conversion to permanent status. Goal: reduce hiring risk for niche senior IC roles, accelerate ramp, and set clear evaluation criteria for managers and people-ops.

Audience:
Hiring managers, people-ops partners, interview panel members, hiring committee.

When to use the bridge-hire flow:
- Role has high ramp uncertainty (new stack, ambiguous ownership).
- Budget constraints or headcount freeze that allow contract-to-hire conversion.
- Need to validate cross-functional fit (platform/infra overlap).
- Candidate prefers trial period or relocation needs a staged commitment.

Protocol summary (high level):
1) Offer stage: candidate receives a 60-90 day bridge offer with clear conversion criteria and a capped conversion timeline. Compensation includes prorated benefits + a conversion bonus on successful transition.
2) Onboarding: 30-day accelerated onboarding checklist (see below). Assign mentor and success owner.
3) Ongoing evaluation: weekly 1:1s + formal 30/60/90 check-ins with rubric scores. People-ops and Hiring Manager jointly own the conversion recommendation.
4) Outcome: convert, extend, or end engagement. Final decision documented with evidence (work samples, rubric scores, manager notes).

Offer template highlights (talking points for recruiter):
- Duration: 60-day trial (standard) or 90-day for complex roles.
- Conversion criteria: competency milestones, peer feedback, shipping one scoped improvement or feature, cultural fit signals.
- Compensation: base rate (contract or provisional perm rate), paid time off pro rata, conversion bonus of 10% of first-month perm salary on conversion.
- Notice and exit: 2-week mutual notice if ending early.

Interview rubric (used for final eval at 30/60/90):
Scoring: 1-5 scale, with 3 = meets expectation for role level; 4 = exceeds; 2 = needs development; 1 = significant gap; 5 = exceptional.
Core dimensions (score each):
- Technical competency: correctness, architecture choices, troubleshooting.
- Delivery and ownership: moves projects forward, unblockers, follow-through.
- Cross-team collaboration: docs, code reviews, communication with PMs/SRE.
- Learning agility: adapts to stack, learns systems quickly.
- Impact during trial: measurable outcome (PRs merged, perf improvement, bug triage).
- Cultural/behavioural fit: feedback from peers, communication, psychological safety.

Rubric guidance notes:
- A candidate with two or more dimensions at 1-2 at 60-day is a high risk for conversion.
- At 30-day, look for trajectory (is the candidate closing gaps?). Evidence matters: link to PRs, design notes, paired session logs.

Sample interview/assessment evidence to collect during trial:
- First-merge PR demonstrating candidate code (link + short summary).
- Simple owned mini-project: defined scope, acceptance criteria, and measurable signal (latency, reliability, improved test coverage).
- Peer feedback form: 3 peers fill a 5-question form after 30/60 days.
- Manager log: weekly note with clear blockers and interventions.

Accelerated onboarding checklist (30-day sprint):
Day 0-3:
- IT access, workstation, repo access, VPN, KMS notes — confirm by EOD day 1.
- Assign mentor and success owner (not the hiring manager).
- Share team goals, current roadmap, and 60-day target.
Day 4-14:
- Shadow 2 key cross-team calls (sre/infra, product sync).
- Complete 1 small triage or bug fix task with mentor pairing.
- Read parity doc pack: architecture overview, runbooks, deploy flow.
Day 15-30:
- Deliver first scoped mini-project.
- Present short walkthrough to team and collect feedback.
- 30-day check: manager and people-ops meet to record rubric scores and decide adjustments.

30/60/90 evaluation cadence and owners:
- Weekly: manager check-ins (documented), mentor feedback.
- 30-day: formative review — focus on ramp blockers and re-scoping if needed. People-ops checks for process adherence.
- 60-day: summative recommendation typically due. If on 90-day flow, 60-day is mid-review documentation point.
- 90-day: final conversion decision. Decision recorded in HRIS + candidate notified.

Conversion decision matrix (simplified):
- Convert: majority of rubric dimensions >= 3 and clear trajectory in lower-scoring areas. Evidence: merged work + peer feedback.
- Extend: marginal scores, but improvement trajectory and high manager confidence. Extension windows: single 30-day extension maximum.
- Decline: persistent 1-2 scores in critical dimensions or negative peer feedback flagged.

Manager playbook (actions to take each week):
- Week 1: 3 short check-ins: kickoff, technical pairing, culture sync. Add notes to rubric doc.
- Weeks 2-4: ensure at least 2 code reviews with actionable comments; remove blockers proactively.
- Weeks 4-8: ensure candidate given at least one end-to-end ownership experience.
- Escalation: if candidate underperforms at 30-day, people-ops will convene a remediation huddle with hiring manager and mentor.

Risk mitigation strategies (people-ops):
- Pre-offer: include role-based test or short take-home to validate core skills where appropriate.
- Contractual: limit bridge-term to a clearly defined scope and include conversion bonus to align incentives.
- Evidence collection: mandate at least 3 artifacts for conversion (PR, design doc, peer feedback).
- Hiring committee oversight: any recommendation to extend or convert a bridge hire for senior roles triggers a 1:1 with Dir/Head of Eng for sign-off.

Communication templates (short):
- Candidate acceptance ack: "Thanks — we will share onboarding schedule and first-week goals by EOD. Your mentor is <name>."
- 30-day formative note: "Thanks for the progress — attached are the 30-day notes. We see strong traction in X, still working on Y. Plan: ..."
- Final conversion: "Congratulations — based on trial results we are converting you to permanent staff effective <date>. Welcome!"

Unresolved questions / items for hiring committee:
- Standardize conversion bonus as percent versus flat amount for parity across levels. (open)
- Should level calibration calls be required for L5+ bridge hires? (open)
- Template for peer feedback form: current version needs simplification. (action: Priya to draft v2)

Quick links and artifacts to attach for each bridge hire file:
- Offer letter + bridge terms (pdf)
- 30/60/90 rubric snapshot (google doc link)
- Evidence bundle: PRs, design notes, peer forms (zip or links)
- Final recommendation memo to HRIS (one paragraph)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this lean; people hate paperwork mid-trial. Focus on evidence and manager coaching.
- For infra roles, prioritize operational readiness metrics instead of feature shipping.
- Check with legal about contractor classification for 90-day trial in EMEA.

Appendix: sample 5-question peer feedback form (free-text encouraged):
1) What did the candidate contribute that helped you?
2) Where did they demonstrate technical judgement?
3) Any collaboration or communication concerns?
4) Rate overall readiness for perm role (1-5) and short rationale.
5) Any red flags or follow-up suggestions?

End of doc.

-- Ayesha
People Ops (owner)
